findings.title: All-groups VIEW is treated as manage
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() gates creating a group and moving an existing group to the top level with requireManage(), which only calls this no-arg canManage(). A principal granted only view-all-groups can therefore create groups and reparent any group to the top of the tree. Per-group canManage(GroupModel) correctly checks MANAGE only, so this is not the same as the view-implies-read checks. The new interface javadoc repeats the VIEW-or-MANAGE wording and should not be treated as the intended contract; the evaluation test states that creating a group requires the manage scope.

findings.title: View-members group id lookup returns the wrong ids
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() is what UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource pass to user search and getUsersCount as membership constraints (session attribute UserModel.GROUPS). The V2 implementation does two things that make those ids unusable. It asks resourceStore.findByType for type "Groups", but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() never calls setType on the per-group resource it creates (only the synthetic all-groups resource is typed), so individual group resources are not returned. For whatever is returned it calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). Authorization resource ids are not group ids; V2 stores the group id as the resource name (resolveGroup returns group.getId(), and hasPermission looks that up with findByName). The permission check therefore misses the group resource and falls back to the all-groups resource, and any ids that are added do not match membership rows. Result: an admin with VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on specific groups gets an empty set (user counts stay 0 or unrestricted, and search is not limited to those groups), while the same scopes on all groups inject non-group ids and the search pre-filter drops every user before canView() can allow them. The new GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest only covers per-group user search, which still passes via the post-filter when the set is empty, so this path is untested.

findings.title: Group deletion hits UnsupportedOperationException or leaks authz resources
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (and the other GroupPermissionManagement methods) always throw UnsupportedOperationException. AdminPermissions.registerListener still handles GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent by calling management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. This PR makes MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() return GroupPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, so a server with both features on will throw from that listener during realm.removeGroup. Provider event listeners are not swallowed, so deleting a group fails with a 500 and the removal is rolled back. If only the V2 feature is on, the listener is not registered at all, and nothing deletes the admin-permissions resource whose name is the group id, so group permissions survive as orphans after the group is gone.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients never gain Groups scopes or the type resource
findings.body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set, and that is the only place this PR creates the Groups resource-type resource and the new scopes manage-membership, manage-members, and view-members. Realms that already enabled admin permissions V2 (the client was created when the schema only had Users and Clients) are not updated. getOrCreateResource then fails with ModelException("No scopes found.") when a group permission is saved, because those scope names are missing. GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission falls back to getResourceTypeResource(..., "Groups"), which returns null, and policyStore.findByResource(server, null) / resource.getScopes() throws NullPointerException. Any fine-grained admin who can list groups but does not hold MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS hits that path from canView(GroupModel), so group listing 500s instead of being filtered.

findings.title: Group permission resources have no display name
findings.body: getResourceName() only resolves a human-readable name for the Users resource type. Group resources created by getOrCreateResource are named with the group id and never get a display name. For a Groups policy the method therefore returns resource.getDisplayName(), which is null. Permission listings in the admin API/UI cannot show which group a permission applies to, unlike users, where the username is resolved from the same resource name.

findings.title: requireManageMembers javadoc cites the wrong check
findings.body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws when canManageMembership(GroupModel) is false. The implementation throws when canManageMembers is false. Those are different scopes (manage-membership vs manage-members). Callers reading only the interface will enforce or test the wrong permission. The new getGroupIdsWithViewPermission javadoc has the same problem: it says it returns a Stream of groups with view permission, but the method returns a Set and both implementations select groups by view-members/manage-members, not view.
